question.prompt: How many real numbers \(x\) satisfy the equation \(3^{2x+2}-3^{x+3}-3^x+3=0?\)

solutions.explanation:
The exponents involve both \(x\) and \(2x\), suggesting that we treat \(3^x\) as one quantity. Let \(t=3^x\), noting that \(t>0\) for every real \(x\). The power laws give
\[
3^{2x+2}=9t^2,
\qquad
3^{x+3}=27t.
\]
Thus the original equation is equivalent to
\[
\begin{aligned}
9t^2-28t+3&=0,\\
(9t-1)(t-3)&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The only possibilities are \(t=1/9\) and \(t=3\), and both satisfy the required condition \(t>0\).

Since \(1/9=3^{-2}\) and \(3=3^1\), these give \(x=-2\) and \(x=1\). The function \(3^x\) is strictly increasing, so each value of \(t\) corresponds to exactly one real \(x\). All transformations were equivalent, so these are exactly the two solutions. The answer is \(\boxed{2}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Turn the equation into a quadratic
